title: Specify physical wire binding and initialization of classical pseudo-locations
description: Contract gap in ISA 0.9 §4.7/§11.1 K24-K25. Normative examples 7 and 10 read an i2 classical argument as a pseudo-location in lift.add. Published lift.add and value helpers take wire formals; K24 value bindings forbid implicit conversion. K25 construction State ordering omits classical pseudo-location storage and permits nonzero initial values only for specified counters/table. No deterministic allocation/initialization/cost/ordinal rule provides the immutable bit wires. An adapter cannot guess per-read temporary wires, global argument storage or constant-control pruning while consumers must charge identical generated leaves and ref.removable is empty. Reproduction: root @g/@ginv examples reach src/oracle.rs::read on Binding::Value and return the explicit postponed diagnostic, while token/classical values forward intact through lproc metadata. Proposed exact text: In the construction State list, after the optional layout counters/mem/stack and before locations in global id order, include one clean class-any storage record for every bit-readable oracle args parameter in declaration order, then every reached lproc instance classical parameter in index-space instance and declaration order. Width is N for iN, ptr_width for ptr, 64 for f64; initial is its canonical unsigned bit-vector value (binary64 bits for f64), I is empty. Token parameters allocate no wires. These immutable storages bind pseudo-location reads to their ordered bits, contribute ordinary scratch occupancy/gates, and contribute no source rows, location IDs, stack cells or R_f terms. Forwarding an entry value through distinct instance keys uses distinct records even for equal values. The existing State initialization and reversed release apply, without basis pruning. Amend K25 nonzero-initial exception to include these storages and add their first-allocation-order frame.scratch records. Add full-tuple/cost/ordinal vectors for i2=0/3, ptr and binary64 negative-zero/NaN bits. Catalog oracle.construct already supports these descriptor widths/initials, so catalog bytes/hash need not change. Queue for ISA filing under COMMON14; keep doing all independent work.

description: ISA0.9 §11 has interface_vertices only when topology is present; generated alloc entries cannot name root interface slots. Current fix retains reproducible defaults and rejects that unencodable choice; selecting b remains required scope once the contract supplies a channel. Exact proposed text: add optional interface_classes:[<concrete target class>,...] to the schedule top level, with one item per prepended inherited-control wire then source interface slot in §9.4 order. Every item names a declared class; each bundle/region is uniform in that class. Resolve these classes before capacity/gate matching; callees inherit actual operand classes. Without this field and without topology, use §11 first-capacity defaults in that order; with interface_vertices each array determines the slot class and all its vertices must agree. When both fields occur they MUST agree; unknown classes, lengths, inconsistent vertices or capacity failures reject. Allocation entries retain their existing scope. title: Specify certificate frames for one closure with differing invocation classes

Neither a class wildcard nor duplicate mut:0 slots is admitted. One descriptor cannot describe both actual invocations. Reproduction: tests/pipeline.rs::context_varying_frame_classes_are_explicitly_deferred_instead_of_misreported. This blocks a complete certificate for a valid mixed-class request, independently of enz.

Proposed exact normative text replacing the required frame entry in §12.3: "Each region record MUST contain exactly one of frame or frame_contexts. frame is the §9.4 descriptor shared by every realised invocation context of that region. frame_contexts is an array of {context: <fully resolved §12.1 invocation context key>, frame: <§9.4 descriptor>}, in increasing bytewise order of JCS context encodings. It MUST contain exactly one record for every realised context, with no duplicates or omissions. The checker selects that context record before instantiating c and checks its classes, widths, lifetimes and interfaces against that realised invocation. A uniform descriptor MUST NOT replace descriptors that differ by classes or resolved parameter/budget-dependent widths." Add frame_contexts?: [...] to the §12.3 region schema, make frame conditional on the exactly-one rule, and add the two-class flip witness to suite F/H. Existing uniform frame records retain their format.

title: Borrowed wires charged as new wires instead of replacing the idle owner's charge
description: Caller with idle y calling a borrowing callee: capacity 3 gives INFEASIBLE; capacity 8, dirty_rate 0.5 gives peak 4 and occupancy 14, while §8.2 ('replacing the owner's charge') with §9.4 idle-set borrowing gives peak 3, occupancy 10. Contestable: the source has no operand naming the idle owner, so this may be a contract gap (then a spec bead naming the field is needed). Estimate agrees with sched on root borrow rows, so agreement is not evidence. Reproduces at HEAD 7f9ceb5: s5_borrow_from_idle_caller_wire_needs_no_extra_capacity and s5_occupancy_replaces_owner_charge red. Probe: bennett-sched/.tmp/opus-reviews/probe/tests/probe.rs (crate depends on the review worktree checked out at 7f9ceb5); run with CARGO_TARGET_DIR=.tmp/opus-reviews/target cargo test --offline -j2 --test probe. Review: docs/reviews/2026-11-02-design-review.md (S5).
notes: Reproduced through the current cdylib C ABI (debug/deps/libbennett_sched.so): capacity3 returns INFEASIBLE; capacity8 reports time4, peak4, occupancy14 at dirty_rate0.5, failing the review expected peak3/occupancy10 assertion. Current allocator creates a distinct dirty requirement; it never records an owner alias, so this is absent lending/owner selection, not merely subtracting a duplicate interval. §9.4 requires a caller-designated idle set and §8.2 replaces an identified owner charge, but §11 alloc carries only class/vertices, no owner identity or default idle-set designation. Exact borrow_from wire-reference/default proposal queued for ISA filing under COMMON14; no unsupported owner field or guessed charge reduction is emitted. This remains required capability and open pending a contract decision plus owner-ledger implementation; independent review/ISA work continues.
